{"timeline":[{"headline":"Phoenician Civilization","text":"Lebanon was part of the ancient Phoenician civilization, which thrived from around 2500 BCE to 539 BCE. The Phoenicians were known for their maritime trading culture and the spread of the Phoenician alphabet.","date":"-2500"},{"headline":"Conquest by the Achaemenid Empire","text":"In 539 BCE, Lebanon came under the control of the Achaemenid Empire after the conquest of the region by Cyrus the Great.","date":"-0539"},{"headline":"Conquest by Alexander the Great","text":"In 332 BCE, Alexander the Great conquered the region, bringing Lebanon under the control of the Macedonian Empire.","date":"-0332"},{"headline":"Roman Rule","text":"Lebanon became part of the Roman Empire in 64 BCE after the Roman general Pompey annexed the region.","date":"-0064"},{"headline":"Byzantine Rule","text":"After the division of the Roman Empire, Lebanon became part of the Byzantine Empire in 395 CE.","date":"0395"},{"headline":"Islamic Conquest","text":"In 636 CE, Lebanon was conquered by the Rashidun Caliphate during the early Islamic conquests.","date":"0636"},{"headline":"Crusader States","text":"During the First Crusade, the Crusaders established several states in the region, including the County of Tripoli, from 1109 to 1289 CE.","date":"1109"},{"headline":"Mamluk Rule","text":"The Mamluks took control of Lebanon in 1291 CE after defeating the Crusaders.","date":"1291"},{"headline":"Ottoman Rule","text":"Lebanon became part of the Ottoman Empire in 1516 CE after the defeat of the Mamluks.","date":"1516"},{"headline":"Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate","text":"In 1861, the Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate was established as a semi-autonomous region within the Ottoman Empire, following the 1860 civil conflict.","date":"1861"},{"headline":"French Mandate","text":"Following World War I and the collapse of the Ottoman Empire, Lebanon was placed under French mandate in 1920.","date":"1920"},{"headline":"Independence from France","text":"Lebanon gained independence from France on November 22, 1943, following a series of political negotiations and the end of the French mandate.","date":"1943-11-22"},{"headline":"Lebanese Civil War","text":"The Lebanese Civil War lasted from 1975 to 1990, resulting in significant political and social changes in the country.","date":"1975"},{"headline":"Taif Agreement","text":"In 1989, the Taif Agreement was signed, marking the end of the Lebanese Civil War and leading to political reforms.","date":"1989"},{"headline":"Cedar Revolution","text":"In 2005, the Cedar Revolution took place, leading to the withdrawal of Syrian troops from Lebanon after a 29-year presence.","date":"2005"}]}
